items.content_excerpt: Kairos Power secured $643 million in combined private and government financing to support construction of its advanced nuclear reactor demonstration project in Tennessee, according to Bloomberg. The funding includes $368 million from private investors, including Google Ventures, DCVC, and Samsung C&T, which contributed $70 million through a partnership announced last month, alongside $275 million from the U.S. Department of Energy. The company is developing advanced nuclear reactors that use molten salt as a coolant instead of water. Most of the funding will support Hermes 2, a 50-megawatt demonstration reactor in Tennessee that Kairos expects to bring online in 2030. Part of the capital will also expand manufacturing capabilities at its facility in New Mexico. Kairos previously signed an agreement to sell electricity to the Tennessee Valley Authority to supply data centers operated by Google, owned by Alphabet. $GOOGL $GOOG
